case.display_title: Tired, off his food and losing weight

consult_notes.note_text: Asked to see a 37-year-old man with a month of fatigue, anorexia and weight loss, and a haemolytic picture with thrombocytopenia. We reviewed the counts, haemolysis markers, coagulation and antiglobulin tests in the Chart so far. Haemolysis with thrombocytopenia and red cell fragments means a thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura must be considered and excluded. Some features are unusual for it, however: if the MCV is high, the reticulocyte response poor, the white count low and the LDH very high out of proportion, a marrow production problem with fragmentation is more likely than a consumptive microangiopathy. Renal function and clotting argue against HUS and DIC. Happy to review again with the results.
recommendations: Ask for the blood film to be reviewed by a haematopathologist, looking at the nucleated red cells and the neutrophils as well as the fragments
Send serum B12 and folate now, before any transfusion or vitamin treatment
Store a citrated sample for ADAMTS13 activity before any plasma is given
Take a full diet history, including how often he eats meat, fish, eggs and dairy
Do not transfuse platelets unless he bleeds; transfuse red cells only for symptoms

consult_notes.note_text: Asked to advise on haemolysis with thrombocytopenia and fragmentation; the Chart now shows megaloblastic nucleated red cells or a megaloblastic marrow. A severe megaloblastic process causes ineffective erythropoiesis with intramedullary haemolysis, a very high LDH, pancytopenia and red cell fragmentation, and can closely mimic a thrombotic microangiopathy. The dysplastic features are expected in this setting and are not evidence of a myelodysplastic neoplasm. Plasma exchange is not indicated on this picture while the vitamin levels are awaited. Happy to review again with the results.
recommendations: Make sure serum B12 and folate were sent before treatment
Start parenteral B12 replacement once the samples are taken; do not give folic acid alone
Transfuse red cells slowly for symptomatic anaemia
Monitor potassium and the reticulocyte count over the first week of treatment
Take a diet history and send intrinsic factor and parietal cell antibodies

consult_notes.note_text: Asked to advise; the Chart now includes a serum B12 of 56 pmol/L (172-675). This very low B12, with the megaloblastic features, accounts for the anaemia, thrombocytopenia, leucopenia, haemolysis and red cell fragmentation. The fragmentation and haemolysis should settle with replacement; there is no indication for plasma exchange or immunosuppression, and the marrow dysplasia should not be labelled as myelodysplasia. The cause still needs to be established. Happy to review again with the results.
recommendations: Continue parenteral B12 replacement
Look for the cause: diet history, intrinsic factor and parietal cell antibodies, and past gastric or ileal surgery
Dietetic advice if intake of animal foods is low
Repeat the blood count, reticulocytes, LDH and potassium during the first week; expect a reticulocyte response by days 5 to 7
Review the counts at four to six weeks, with the blood film

consult_notes.note_text: Seen for a dietary assessment. He is not vegetarian or vegan but eats meat or seafood only about once a month; most meals are rice, noodles and vegetables, with occasional eggs and little dairy. Appetite has been poor for a month. Intake of animal foods is well below recommended amounts. Happy to review again.
recommendations: Eat meat, fish, eggs or dairy daily; practical options for a busy working day discussed
Consider fortified foods
Review intake at follow-up alongside the blood results

consult_notes.note_text: Asked about a gastrointestinal cause for his anaemia and weight loss. No abdominal pain, dysphagia, dyspepsia, change in bowel habit or bleeding; no previous gastrointestinal surgery; no acid-suppressing or other medicines. Abdomen soft with no masses or organomegaly. We see no gastrointestinal red flags. If a malabsorptive cause is being considered, the first steps are serological. Happy to review again with the results.
recommendations: Intrinsic factor and parietal cell antibodies
Coeliac serology (tTG-IgA with total IgA)
Helicobacter pylori stool antigen
Upper GI endoscopy with gastric body and duodenal biopsies only if the antibodies are positive or new symptoms appear

consult_notes.note_text: Asked to assess for neurological involvement. No numbness, paraesthesiae, unsteadiness, visual or cognitive symptoms. On examination: cranial nerves normal; tone, power and reflexes normal with flexor plantars; joint position, vibration and pinprick sensation intact; Romberg negative; gait normal. No neurological deficit. Happy to review if symptoms develop.
recommendations: No neuroimaging or nerve studies needed at present
Check serum B12 and folate if not already sent, and avoid nitrous oxide until they are known
Re-examine at follow-up

consult_notes.note_text: Asked about renal involvement in a possible thrombotic microangiopathy. Creatinine 64 umol/L with eGFR 99; normal urine output; blood pressure normal; urinalysis bland with no blood or protein. There is no evidence of renal thrombotic microangiopathy or hypertensive injury. Happy to review if renal function changes.
recommendations: Monitor creatinine and urine output
No renal indication for plasma exchange

consult_notes.note_text: Asked about an underlying malignancy as a cause of a microangiopathic picture with weight loss. No lymphadenopathy, organomegaly, bone pain or focal symptoms. We would expect a cancer-related microangiopathy to show a leucoerythroblastic film and marrow infiltration. Happy to review again with the results.
recommendations: Bone marrow examination if the cause of the cytopenias remains unclear
Imaging only if the marrow or clinical findings point to a malignancy

consult_notes.note_text: Asked about a connective tissue disease. No joint pain, rash, photosensitivity, mouth ulcers or Raynaud's; examination shows no synovitis or skin changes. Nothing clinically to suggest lupus or another connective tissue disease. Happy to review with autoantibody results.
recommendations: ANA and complement if not already sent

consult_notes.note_text: Asked about an infective cause of haemolysis and cytopenias. Afebrile, no travel in the past year, no risk factors for blood-borne viruses and no unwell contacts. Infection seems unlikely. Happy to review with the results.
recommendations: HIV, hepatitis B and C serology as a baseline
Malaria testing is not needed without travel or fever

consult_notes.note_text: Asked about tachycardia and a systolic murmur. Resting sinus tachycardia and a soft ejection systolic murmur fit a high-output state from severe anaemia; no chest pain, no signs of heart failure, troponin normal. Echocardiogram, if done, would be expected to show a hyperdynamic ventricle with normal valves. No primary cardiac problem. Happy to review if new problems arise.
recommendations: Transfuse slowly, one unit at a time, with a fluid balance chart
No cardiac investigation needed beyond the ECG

Serum B12 and folate sent before transfusion or treatment; ADAMTS13 stored or sent

Cause sought: diet, intrinsic factor and parietal cell antibodies; dietary advice

secondary_findings: Thrombocytopenia and later leucopenia (pancytopenia) from ineffective haematopoiesis, recovering with treatment
Dysplastic marrow features (dyserythropoiesis, dysmegakaryopoiesis) from B12 deficiency, with a normal karyotype: not a myelodysplastic neoplasm
Raised serum iron and ferritin with ineffective erythropoiesis and haemolysis; no iron deficiency
final_dx.text: Vitamin B12 deficiency from low dietary intake of animal foods, presenting as pseudo-thrombotic microangiopathy: haemolytic anaemia with massive schistocytosis, thrombocytopenia, a very high LDH, macrocytosis, circulating megaloblasts and a megaloblastic marrow

key_discriminators: reticulocytes 44.8 x10^9/L: inadequate response for the degree of haemolysis
megaloblastic nucleated red cells on the reviewed film
normal coagulation apart from a slightly raised D-dimer
negative direct and indirect antiglobulin tests
diet: meat or seafood about once a month
megaloblastic marrow with a normal karyotype
red cell histogram peak around 10 fL (fragments)

must_do.text: Take a diet history, including how often he eats meat, fish, eggs and dairy
Send serum B12 (or active B12) and folate before transfusion or vitamin treatment
Have the blood film reviewed for megaloblastic nucleated red cells and hypersegmented neutrophils, not only schistocytes
Recognise that a high MCV, a poor reticulocyte response, leucopenia and a disproportionately high LDH argue against TTP
Start parenteral B12 replacement promptly once the deficiency is likely and the samples are taken
Look for the cause of the deficiency, including intrinsic factor antibodies for pernicious anaemia
Give dietary advice, or refer to a dietitian, to correct the low intake of animal foods
Follow the blood count, reticulocytes, LDH and potassium to confirm the response to treatment

must_not_do.text: Start plasma exchange or rituximab (or place a central line for plasma exchange) when the picture is explained by the vitamin deficiency
Diagnose a myelodysplastic neoplasm on marrow dysplasia before excluding B12 and folate deficiency
Give folic acid alone without B12
Transfuse platelets in the absence of bleeding while a thrombotic microangiopathy is not excluded

ground_truth.outcome: Discharged on day 7 with improving symptoms (Hb 88 g/L, platelets 48 x10^9/L, WBC 3.2 x10^9/L, LDH 1353 U/L). Five weeks after presentation (day 35, outside the playable admission): Hb 131 g/L (printed 13.1 g/dL), MCV 91.5 fL, platelets 219 x10^9/L, WBC 10.2 x10^9/L, LDH 211 U/L, B12 277 pmol/L (printed 375 pg/mL); schistocytes gone and analyser histograms normal. The authors attribute the deficiency to diet rather than pernicious anaemia.
red_herrings: dyserythropoiesis and dysmegakaryopoiesis in the marrow

rubric.text: Vitamin B12 deficiency with low intake of animal foods identified as the cause
Vitamin B12 deficiency, cause not identified
Pernicious anaemia, megaloblastic anaemia unspecified or mixed nutritional anaemia as the final diagnosis
TTP, HUS or another thrombotic microangiopathy, DIC, myelodysplasia, folate deficiency, autoimmune haemolysis or disseminated cancer as the final diagnosis
Unrelated diagnosis, or one that would lead to harm

teaching_points: B12 deficiency can mimic thrombotic microangiopathy (pseudo-TMA), with schistocytes, thrombocytopenia and a very high LDH
Features favouring B12 deficiency over TTP: high MCV, low reticulocytes, leucopenia, very high LDH, megaloblasts on the film
A PLASMIC score in the intermediate range does not settle the question
ADAMTS13 takes days to return; the film and indices, available within hours, can steer away from plasma exchange (the authors did not send it)
Send B12 and folate before treatment: a single injection makes the serum B12 uninterpretable
Analyser red cell and platelet histograms can support the detection of schistocytes and track their clearance
ground_truth.treatment_given: Red cell transfusion on day 1 for severe exertional breathlessness, then intramuscular cyanocobalamin from day 1 on suspicion of B12 deficiency (after the marrow). ADAMTS13 activity was considered but not sent; no plasma exchange. Serum B12 76 pg/mL (56 pmol/L) reported on day 4. Cyanocobalamin injections stopped at discharge on day 7; dietary advice to eat meat. Intrinsic factor and parietal cell antibodies were not tested (not covered by national health insurance in Japan).

raw_material.findings: Hypercellular marrow. Marked megaloblastic change throughout erythroid maturation, with fine chromatin evenly distributed through the nucleus. reports.impression: Marked red cell fragmentation with macrocytosis, nucleated red cells and thrombocytopenia.
reports.report_text: Red cells: marked anisopoikilocytosis with numerous red cell fragments (schistocytes); many macrocytes. Nucleated red cells present (about 6 per 100 white cells). No spherocytes or agglutination. White cells: reduced to low-normal in number. Platelets: reduced, confirmed on the film; no clumps. Comment: marked red cell fragmentation with thrombocytopenia; urgent review by a haematopathologist recommended.
reports.status_line: Screening film reported by a biomedical scientist. A haematopathologist review can be requested.

reports.impression: Marked red cell fragmentation; megaloblastic nucleated red cells with dysplastic features; hypersegmented neutrophils; oval macrocytes; thrombocytopenia.
reports.report_text: Film reviewed by a haematopathologist. Red cells: marked anisopoikilocytosis with numerous schistocytes; oval macrocytes; no spherocytes, no agglutination, no polychromasia of note. Nucleated red cells about 6 per 100 white cells, several with dysplastic features: nuclear fragmentation, nuclear atypia and large erythroblasts with finely dispersed, open chromatin (megaloblastic nuclear pattern). White cells: hypersegmented neutrophils, some with six or more lobes. No blasts. Platelets: reduced; no clumps. Comment: red cell fragmentation together with a megaloblastic picture in the nucleated red cells and neutrophils. Suggest serum B12 and folate before any transfusion or vitamin treatment. ADAMTS13 activity may be sent if a thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura remains a concern.
reports.status_line: Final report, reviewed by a haematopathologist.

reports.impression: Hypercellular marrow with marked megaloblastic change and trilineage dysplastic features; no excess of blasts; no infiltrate.
reports.report_text: Particulate aspirate, hypercellular. Erythropoiesis is expanded and shows marked megaloblastic change throughout maturation, with fine chromatin evenly dispersed through large nuclei and nuclear-cytoplasmic asynchrony; irregular nuclei and multinucleated erythroblasts are present. Granulopoiesis: giant metamyelocytes and band forms, and hypersegmented and giant neutrophils. Megakaryocytes are present with separated, multinucleated forms. Blasts 1%. No abnormal infiltrate. Comment: megaloblastic erythropoiesis with dysplastic features in all three lineages. Suggest serum B12 and folate; dysplasia of this kind should not be taken as evidence of a myelodysplastic neoplasm until these are known. See the karyotype.

reports.impression: Hypercellular marrow with erythroid hyperplasia; no fibrosis and no infiltrate.
reports.report_text: Adequate trephine core (18 mm). Hypercellular for age (about 80%) with marked erythroid expansion and left-shifted, immature-looking erythropoiesis. Granulopoiesis and megakaryocytes present in normal numbers; some large megakaryocytes. No fibrosis (reticulin grade 0). No granulomas and no infiltrate by lymphoma or carcinoma. No increase in CD34-positive cells.

reports.impression: Increased storage iron; no ring sideroblasts.
reports.report_text: Perls stain. Storage iron increased (grade 4) in marrow fragments. Many erythroblasts contain coarse siderotic granules; no ring sideroblasts are seen.

reports.impression: No excess of blasts and no abnormal population; erythroid expansion.
reports.report_text: Erythroid precursors increased, with a raised proportion of early (CD117-positive, CD71-bright) forms. Myeloid maturation shows mild asynchrony without an aberrant immunophenotype. CD34-positive blasts 0.8% with a normal phenotype. B cells polyclonal; plasma cells polyclonal. No abnormal population detected.

reports.impression: No abnormality detected with the myelodysplasia FISH panel.
reports.report_text: Two hundred interphase nuclei scored per probe. Normal signal patterns for 5q31, 7q31, chromosome 8 centromere and 20q12; no deletion or gain detected.

reports.impression: No pathogenic variant detected.
reports.report_text: Targeted sequencing of a myeloid gene panel achieved adequate coverage across all regions. No pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants were detected at a variant allele frequency of 2% or more.

reports.impression: No abnormal population in the blood.
reports.report_text: Lymphocytes comprise a polyclonal mixture of T, B and NK cells with normal antigen expression. B cells show a normal kappa to lambda ratio. No blasts or abnormal populations. Granulocytes and monocytes express CD55 and CD59 normally.

reports.impression: Normal chest radiograph.
reports.report_text: PA erect chest radiograph. The heart size and mediastinal contours are within normal limits. The lungs are clear and both costophrenic angles are sharp. No hilar enlargement. No bony abnormality.

reports.impression: Normal CT chest.
reports.report_text: CT of the chest with contrast. The lungs are clear with no nodules, consolidation or interstitial change. The airways are patent. No mediastinal, hilar or axillary lymph node enlargement. No pleural or pericardial effusion. No bone lesion.

reports.impression: Normal CT abdomen and pelvis; spleen not enlarged.
reports.report_text: Contrast-enhanced CT of the abdomen and pelvis in the portal venous phase. The liver, spleen (11 cm), pancreas, adrenal glands and kidneys are normal. The stomach and bowel are unremarkable. No lymph node enlargement, mass or free fluid. No bone lesion.

reports.impression: Normal abdominal ultrasound; spleen not enlarged.
reports.report_text: The liver is normal in size and echotexture with no focal lesion. The gallbladder is thin-walled without calculi and the common bile duct is not dilated. The spleen is normal in size (10.8 cm). The pancreas, where seen, is normal. Both kidneys are normal in size with no hydronephrosis. No free fluid.

reports.impression: Normal CT head.
reports.report_text: Non-contrast CT of the head. Grey-white matter differentiation is preserved. No intracranial haemorrhage, infarct, mass effect or midline shift. The ventricles and sulci are normal for age.

reports.impression: Normal upper GI endoscopy and biopsies; no atrophic body gastritis.
reports.report_text: Endoscopy to the second part of the duodenum. Normal oesophageal, gastric and duodenal mucosa; normal gastric body folds. No ulceration, varices or bleeding. Biopsies from the gastric body and antrum and from the duodenum: normal gastric mucosa with preserved oxyntic glands, no atrophy or intestinal metaplasia, no Helicobacter organisms; normal duodenal villous architecture.

reports.impression: Normal colonoscopy and terminal ileum.
reports.report_text: Complete colonoscopy to the caecum with intubation of the terminal ileum; good bowel preparation. Normal mucosa throughout with no polyps, ulceration or bleeding. Terminal ileum normal.

reports.impression: Normal MRI spine; normal cord signal.
reports.report_text: MRI of the whole spine. Normal vertebral marrow signal and alignment. The spinal cord is of normal calibre and signal throughout, including the dorsal columns of the cervical and thoracic cord. No compression. No disc protrusion of significance.

reports.impression: Normal MRI brain.
reports.report_text: MRI of the brain with diffusion-weighted and post-contrast imaging. Normal grey and white matter signal with no restricted diffusion. The ventricles and sulci are normal. No enhancing lesion.

reports.impression: Normal nerve conduction studies and EMG; no neuropathy.
reports.report_text: Motor and sensory nerve conduction studies of the upper and lower limbs show normal amplitudes, latencies and conduction velocities, including the sural sensory responses. Concentric needle EMG of selected muscles is normal.

reports.impression: Normal renal tract ultrasound.
reports.report_text: Both kidneys are normal in size (right 10.9 cm, left 11.2 cm) with preserved corticomedullary differentiation. No calculi and no pelvicalyceal dilatation. The bladder is unremarkable.

reports.impression: No malarial parasites seen.
reports.report_text: Thick and thin films examined under oil immersion (200 fields). No malarial parasites seen. Incidental: numerous red cell fragments and macrocytes; see the blood film report.

vignette: A 37-year-old man is referred to hospital with a one-month history of fatigue, loss of appetite and weight loss. He has no relevant past medical history and takes no regular medicines.
